subject: Choose to not tape Newton iterations

messages.author: 2650d93cd958f62c
messages.subject: Choose to not tape Newton iterations
parts:
Dear all TMB users


When working with Newton type functions that are dependent on a starting point, I would like to only tape the last two iterations. Is this possible in TMB, to somehow tell TMB to not tape a part of the code?

I provide the following code, which I hope will make the problem clear:


#include<TMB.hpp>


// Newton function

template<class Type, class Functor>

Type newton_local(Functor f, vector<Type> s, int niter) {

    for (int i = 0; i<niter; i++) {

        vector<Type> g = autodiff::gradient(f, s); 

        matrix<Type> H = autodiff::hessian(f, s); 

        s -= atomic::matinv(H) * g;

    }

    return s(0);

}


// 2nd degree polynomial

template<class Type>

struct poly_2{

    Type a, b, c;

    poly_2(Type a_, Type b_, Type c_) : a(a_), b(b_), c(c_) {}

    template<typename T>

    T operator()(vector<T> x){

        T val, a_=T(a), b_=T(b), c_=T(c);

        val = a_*x(0)*x(0) + b_*x(0) + c_;

        return val;

    }

};


template<class Type>

Type objective_function<Type>::operator()()

{

    PARAMETER(a);

    PARAMETER(b);

    PARAMETER(c);

    

    vector<Type> x(1);

    x.setZero(); // reasonable starting point

    poly_2<Type> polly(a, b, c); // 2nd degree polynomial

    int niter = 5; // Newton iterations

    

    // Somehow wrap this so that it is not taped

    x(0) = newton_local(polly, x, niter-2);

    

    // Last two iterations are taped

    x(0) = newton_local(polly, x, 2);

    

    return x.sum();

}


I imagine that some "hacky" version of using TMB_ATOMIC_VECTOR_FUNCTION, where derivatives are only defined with respect to the last two iterations, maybe could help me out.

I apologize in advance, if there already exist some documentation related to this. I have not been able to find such documentation.

All suggestions on how to go about this problem are much appreciated.


Thank you for your time! 

Berent

messages.subject: RE: [TMB users] Choose to not tape Newton iterations
parts:
You are right that this could in principle be implemented using TMB_ATOMIC_VECTOR_FUNCTION.

However, I might suggest a different approach. You could implement the objective like this:

template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator()()
{
    PARAMETER(a);
    PARAMETER(b);
    PARAMETER(c);
PARAMETER_VECTOR(x); // Optionally pass inits
poly_2<Type> polly(a, b, c); // 2nd degree polynomial

if (x.size() == 0) {
      // No inits - get them
      x.resize(1);
x.setZero(); // reasonable starting point
int niter = 5; // Newton iterations
x(0) = newton_local(polly, x, niter-2);

REPORT(x);
      return 0;

}
   
    // Last two iterations are taped
    x(0) = newton_local(polly, x, 2);
   
    return x.sum();
}

And from R construct two objects. The first to get the initial values:

getInits <- MakeADFun(data=list(), parameters=list(a=1,b=1,c=1,x=numeric(0)), type="Fun")
getInits$report(1:3)

The second to do the normal evaluation

obj <- MakeADFun(data=list(), parameters=list(a=1,b=1,c=1,x=numeric(1)))

Then glue these two together to something like:

fn <- function(par) obj$fn(c(par, getInits$report(par)$x))
gr <- function(par) obj$gr(c(par, getInits$report(par)$x))[1:3]

Thank you for the clever solution!

I must admit, that I was not aware of the option to "Run through the template with ordinary double-types" by setting type="Fun".

My real problem involves the saddlepoint approximation, and I find the saddlepoints by using a Newton type function. Since I will have several numerical saddlepoints, I will use your solution to report the vector of initials. This should work fine.

For the Newton method it would be nice to have some error handling, using if-else statements (with respect to functions of parameters of the objective). This has previously not been possible for me, using AD types, but I imagine this will be okay when we run through the templates with double-types? Sorry for this extra question.

Thank you for your time!

Berent

messages.author: 90b303eef43fd993
messages.subject: RE: [TMB users] Choose to not tape Newton iterations
parts:
There is no problem with if-else branches when using double-types.

However, there's a more efficient method you should also be aware of.
Currently, a temporary tape of 3 newton iterations is implicitly created for each 'getInits' evaluation. It would be better to tape a single newton step and store it rather than retaping it for each evaluation. The tape could be iterated from R until a desired tolerance on the gradient is acheived.

You could get this working with some minor modifications to the previous:

* Use ADREPORT instead of REPORT
* Pass ADreport = TRUE to MakeADFun for the 'getInits' tape.
* Set type='ADFun' for the 'getInits' tape.
* Replace "if(x.size()==0)" with "if(flag)" for som flag passed as data.
* Pass niter=1 to newton_local inside the branch.
* x <- getInits$fn(c(a,b,c,x)) should now perform a newton step from R.
